name: Pink-headed Fruit-Dove
rangeDescription: Montane forest of southern sumatra, java, and bali
description: An absolute gem of a dove, found only in high montane forests. Combination of bright pink head, black-and-white chest band, and leaf-green back is unmistakable.

name: Macquarie Shag
rangeDescription: Macquarie island and adjacent bishop and clerk rocks
description: Learn about Imperial Cormorant (Macquarie): explore photos, sounds, and observations collected by birders around the world.

name: Black-headed Heron
rangeDescription: Grassland and savanna of sub-saharan africa
description: A large, grayish heron of drier habitats; note distinctly dark cap and nape contrasting with white throat. In flight the underwing is strongly contrasting black-and-white.

name: Great Potoo
rangeDescription: Far southern mexico to northern bolivia, paraguay, and southeastern brazil
description: A monstrous nightbird, superficially similar to an owl but not related. Pale mottled gray with large head; larger than other potoos and lacks a dark mustache stripe.

name: Moseley's Rockhopper Penguin
rangeDescription: Tristan da cunha, gough, st. paul, and amsterdam islands
description: A small black-and-white penguin with a wild, bushy yellow crest. Marine and variably pelagic, foraging offshore and nesting on boulder-strewn beaches and among stands of tussock grass.

name: Rufous-winged Ground-Cuckoo
rangeDescription: Southern venezuela, guyana, and northern brazil (roraima)
description: Large, terrestrial bird of lowland forest; unlike anything else in range. Appears all dark with paler belly; note long tail, heavy bill, and bare red skin around eye.

name: Silver Oriole
rangeDescription: Mountains of southern china; winters to southern thailand and cambodia
description: Male’s bone-white back and belly are unlike that of any other oriole. Female has the same black head and wings but has a gray-brown back and a densely streaked belly.

name: White-fronted Honeyeater
rangeDescription: Woodland of inland australia, to southern and western coasts
description: Small nomadic honeyeater of the outback, fairly common across arid parts of inland Australia. Mottled gray and brown above, pale with dark streaks below, with bold white forehead, white moustache, black throat and upper chest, and yellow in primary feathers.

name: White-browed Conebill
rangeDescription: Andes of eastern peru (san martín) and western bolivia
description: Tiny bicolored tanager with a sharp, pointed bill. Orangey red below and bluish gray above, with a strong white eyebrow.

name: Northern Rosella
rangeDescription: Kimberley range to northern territory/queensland border
description: Pale yellow rosella with black crown contrasting with white cheeks. The only rosella found in Northern Territory and northwestern Western Australia, where it inhabits open forests and woodlands, often near creeks and streams.

name: Chestnut-capped Puffbird
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia to venezuela, northern bolivia, and western amazonian brazil
description: Attractive small puffbird of lowland rainforest. White below, reddish brown above, with a black mask and single black breast band.

name: Minas Gerais Tyrannulet
rangeDescription: South-central bahia to central minas gerais, in eastern brazil
description: Small flycatcher with a long tail. Olive-green above, yellowish below, with two yellow wingbars.

name: Mongolian Accentor
rangeDescription: Mountains of mongolia and immediately adjacent northern china (ningxia)
description: A very plain accentor of dry, open areas with sparse, scrubby vegetation. Patterning more closely resembles that of a lark or a pipit than another accentor: pale sandy brown all over with a paler belly and a finely streaked back.

name: Brazza's Martin
rangeDescription: Locally along rivers of southwestern democratic republic of the congo and northeastern angola (lunda)
description: A typical martin with brown upperparts and pale underparts strongly marked with dark streaks. Juvenile is rustier, with a paler chin and throat, and is less boldly streaked below.

name: Makira Thrush
rangeDescription: Makira (southeastern solomon islands)
description: Mostly ground-dwelling, rotund and rusty brown. Intricate scaling on breast becomes fainter but denser on throat.

name: New Zealand Storm-Petrel
rangeDescription: New zealand (little barrier island)
description: Small seabird endemic to New Zealand. Dark blackish-brown head, breast, upperparts, and tail.

name: White-billed Starling
rangeDescription: Mountains of eritrea and ethiopia
description: A dark starling with an ivory-colored bill, a dark red eye, and large red panels in the wings. Males have a dark head and females a pale gray one.

name: Olive Finch
rangeDescription: Locally in andes of colombia to ecuador and southeastern peru
description: A shy, stream-loving, finch-like bird of Andean cloud forest. Plumage is olive with a chestnut crown and gray face and throat.

name: Tricolored Blackbird
rangeDescription: Marshes and farmlands of southwestern oregon to northwestern baja california
description: Very similar to Red-winged Blackbird. Male entirely glossy black with red shoulder patch bordered by white, not yellow.

name: Golden-winged Tody-Flycatcher
rangeDescription: Southeastern colombia (putumayo) to eastern ecuador and northeastern peru (loreto)
description: Small, colorful flycatcher found in lowland and foothill rainforest. Ranges primarily in eastern Ecuador, but also reaches adjacent areas of southern Colombia and northern Peru.
